title: Time between train posts
prompt: A train moves at a steady speed past eight posts. Neighbouring posts are 6 metres apart. It takes 18 seconds for the front of the train to go from the first post to the last. What is its speed in metres per second? Give an exact fraction.

title: Start the shorter recording later
prompt: A recorder takes its first reading as soon as it starts and takes another every 8 seconds. It takes nine readings altogether. Another recorder will take only seven readings in the same way. How many seconds later should the second recorder start so they finish together?

title: The pump and the leak
prompt: A pump fills a tank in 42 minutes. A leak alone empties a full tank in 84 minutes. Both rates are constant. How many minutes does the pump take to fill the empty tank while it leaks?

title: One machine's rate is hidden
prompt: Two machines together make 42 pieces each hour. The first makes 14 pieces each hour on its own. How many hours does the second take to make 84 pieces on its own?

title: Distance on each part of the ride
prompt: A cyclist rides for 15 minutes at 28 km/h, stops for 10 minutes and then rides for 30 minutes at 14 km/h. How far does she travel, in kilometres?

title: Average across a return journey
prompt: A hiker walks 14 km at 7 km/h and returns along the same route at 14 km/h. What is the average speed for the full journey in kilometres per hour? Give an exact fraction.

title: The time it takes to overtake
prompt: Two riders cycle in the same direction at steady speeds. The rider in front is 21 metres ahead and moves at 2 metres per second. The rider behind moves at 5 metres per second. After how many seconds do they draw level?

title: The third meeting around the track
prompt: Two runners start together on a circular track 42 metres long and run in opposite directions at 2 and 4 metres per second. How many seconds after starting do they meet for the third time? The start does not count as a meeting.

title: Two buses use the same road
prompt: A bus travels for 20 minutes at 36 kilometres per hour and then for 10 minutes at 48 kilometres per hour. How many kilometres does it travel altogether?

title: Split the route by distance
prompt: A cyclist rides 24 kilometres. She rides the first 12 kilometres at 12 kilometres per hour and the other 12 at 18 kilometres per hour. What is her average speed over the whole route, in kilometres per hour? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: Two bakers split the batch
prompt: One baker shapes 18 rolls in 6 minutes. Another shapes 20 in 5 minutes. They work at constant rates. How many rolls can they shape together in 12 minutes?

title: A slow drain and two taps
prompt: Two taps working together add 15 litres per minute to a tank. A drain lets out 3 litres per minute. The tank already holds 24 litres. How many minutes will it take to reach 120 litres with both taps and the drain open?

title: One cutter takes a break
prompt: A green cutter cuts 6 shapes per minute and a blue cutter cuts 4 per minute. During a ten-minute job the green cutter runs throughout and the blue cutter rests for the first three minutes. How many shapes do they cut altogether?

title: The second tap opens later
prompt: Tap A adds 4 litres per minute from the start. Tap B adds 3 litres per minute, but opens five minutes later. Both then stay open. After how many minutes from the start will an empty tank hold 62 litres?

title: Two riders close the gap
prompt: Two cyclists start 63 metres apart and ride towards one another. One rides at 3 metres per second and the other at 4 metres per second. How many seconds do they take to meet?

title: One rider pauses
prompt: Two toy cars start 70 metres apart and drive towards one another. The first travels at 3 metres per second. The second travels at 4 metres per second but pauses for two seconds, beginning exactly five seconds after the start. After how many seconds from the start do they meet? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: The slow machine catches up
prompt: A printer prints 10 labels a minute. A second printer starts with 32 labels already printed, then prints 6 a minute. After how many minutes will their label counts be equal?

title: Share the work in thirds
prompt: Maya can paint one board in 12 minutes. Leo can paint an identical board in 18 minutes. Maya paints the first third of one board alone. Then they work together at their constant rates until that board is finished. How many minutes does the whole job take? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: Two different gaps between posts
prompt: A cyclist passes six posts in a straight line. The first three gaps are 12 metres each, and the last two gaps are 8 metres each. The trip from the first post to the sixth takes 13 seconds at a steady speed. What is the speed in metres per second?

title: Red and blue clips on a rope
prompt: A rope has thirteen red clips every 5 metres, including both ends. Blue clips are spaced 4 metres apart on the same rope, also with a clip at each end. How many blue clips are there?

title: The first part takes longer
prompt: A runner covers 3 kilometres in 18 minutes, then rests for 6 minutes before running another 2 kilometres in 12 minutes. What is the average speed including the rest, in kilometres per hour? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: Time behind the planned pace
prompt: A cyclist planned to ride 30 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour. For the first 10 kilometres she only averages 12 kilometres per hour. What speed, in kilometres per hour, must she average for the remaining 20 kilometres to finish at the original planned time? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: Count only the spaces covered
prompt: A roller paints one stripe every 2 seconds, with its first stripe at time 0. At time 28 seconds the last stripe has just been painted. How many stripes are there?

title: The waits on a bus route
prompt: Seven stops lie equally far apart along a route. A bus takes 24 minutes of moving time to travel from the first stop to the last. It waits two minutes at every intermediate stop. How many minutes pass between leaving the first stop and arriving at the last?

title: The second tray finishes later
prompt: Two machines make biscuits at constant rates. The faster makes 8 biscuits a minute and the slower makes 5. They start together on separate batches of 80 biscuits each. How many minutes after the faster machine finishes does the slower one finish?

title: What one worker can do
prompt: A machine and an assistant together pack 120 boxes in 8 minutes. The same machine and two assistants together pack 120 boxes in 6 minutes. All work at constant rates and the assistants work at the same rate. How many boxes does the machine alone pack per minute?

title: One runner laps the other
prompt: Two runners leave the same mark on a 120-metre circular track in the same direction. Their speeds are 5 and 3 metres per second. How many seconds pass before the faster runner first catches the slower runner again?

title: They cross, then turn back
prompt: Two toy trains start 60 metres apart and travel towards one another at 4 and 6 metres per second. When they meet, the slower train immediately reverses and the faster train continues in its original direction. How many seconds after the first meeting will the trains be 14 metres apart?

title: Extra minutes after the leak
prompt: A tap adds 12 litres per minute to an empty tank. For the first 3 minutes a leak lets out 2 litres per minute. The leak is then plugged while the tap keeps running. How many minutes from the start does it take to reach 90 litres?

title: Three taps, three pairs
prompt: Each of three taps adds water at a constant rate. Taps A and B together add 10 litres per minute, A and C add 13, and B and C add 15. How many minutes do all three taps take to add 95 litres?

title: The last fence post is removed
prompt: A 48-metre straight fence has posts every 4 metres, including both ends. One end post and every third remaining post, counted from the opposite end, are removed. How many posts remain?

title: Two cameras capture the same instant
prompt: Two cameras photograph a race at regular intervals. The first takes a picture every 7 seconds starting at time 0. The second takes a picture every 5 seconds starting at time 3. How many seconds pass between the first and third times when both cameras take a picture at the same instant?

title: Compare the two arrival times
prompt: Two cyclists cover the same 24-kilometre route. Mia rides at 12 kilometres per hour with no stops. Pat rides at 16 kilometres per hour and takes a 20-minute rest. How many minutes sooner does the faster finisher arrive?

title: A third of the ride in half the time
prompt: A rider travels 36 kilometres in two hours at two different steady speeds. The first half of the time covers only one-third of the distance. What is the difference between the two speeds, in kilometres per hour?

title: Time between the middle readings
prompt: A machine logs 17 readings at equal intervals, starting at time zero. The seventh reading is at 30 seconds. How many seconds pass between the ninth and seventeenth readings?

title: Gate counts from opposite ends
prompt: Twenty-one equally spaced posts stand along a straight path, including both ends. One walker marks every fourth post from the left, counting the left end as post 1. A second marks every third post from the right, counting the right end as post 1. How many posts get both marks?

title: The chase begins at the bridge
prompt: A runner passes a bridge at 4 metres per second. Five seconds later a cyclist leaves the bridge along the same path at 9 metres per second. How many seconds does the cyclist take to catch the runner after leaving the bridge?

title: The first meeting is not halfway
prompt: Two runners start from the same point on a 180-metre circular track, running in opposite directions. Their first meeting is 72 metres clockwise from the start. The clockwise runner takes 36 seconds to run a full lap. What is the other runner's speed, in metres per second? Give an exact fraction if needed.

title: Distance from the first to the last mark
prompt: An athlete passes 9 equally spaced flags at a steady 5 metres per second. It takes 21 seconds to go from the second flag to the ninth. How many metres apart are neighbouring flags?

title: An extra marker in every other gap
prompt: A line of posts has 21 posts spaced 6 metres apart. A new marker is added at the midpoint of the first gap, the third gap, the fifth gap, and so on. Starting at the first post, how many metres along the line is the 25th object when posts and new markers are counted together?

title: Work back from the final segment
prompt: A cyclist goes 8 kilometres, then covers half the remaining route before taking a break. The last part takes 36 minutes at 15 kilometres per hour. How many kilometres was the full route?

title: The first leg and the last leg
prompt: A cyclist rides for 20 minutes at 15 kilometres per hour. She then rides for half an hour at a different steady speed. At the end her average speed over the full 50 minutes is 18 kilometres per hour. What was her speed in the second part, in kilometres per hour?
